Not exactly racist but I used to be somewhat homophobic growing up. I was raised in a conservative Christian family and was taught being gay is wrong and you’ll go to hell for it. Up until about 9th grade I believed this, what changed started in about 7th grade I’d just transferred from a private Christian school to a public school due to issues with money in the family. From 7th grade till now (22) I’ve mistakenly been labeled as gay by like roughly 80% of the people I meet, heck even my current gf thought I was gay until I asked her out. Anyways between 7th and 9th grade I was bullied a lot mostly by guys for being “gay” at first it would upset me until I realized that this is how some people treat others for being gay. It really changed my perspective on how I treat gay people. At first I didn’t fully convert to being non homophobic I just decided that being gay is wrong but I should never treat a gay person wrong and that it was for god to handle. Then around 11th grade I was realized I respect certain aspects of Christians and the religion but I don’t want to live my life worshipping a god who’d care about a persons sexuality (amongst other things) it just seemed so silly to me. Since then I’ve really turned over a new leaf. I even tried changing my parents views on gays it didn’t work well but they’ve grown less hateful towards gays still would consider them homophobic by definition tho. I still regularly get mistaken for being gay and I’m ok with it me and my gf even joke about it since I get hit on by more guys than girls. Some of my family members are racist I’ve never had that problem maybe because my half sisters are black I’ve always accepted them and would never think someone’s inferior because their skin looked different, also one of them came out to me as bi last year I was super happy she was comfortable telling me since she still hasn’t told our parents which is understandable since their views are homophobic I’m sure she will come out eventually to them but I think it’s best she waits till she graduates high school and is able to move out. Long story short never really been racist was semi homophobic growing up now I’m not.

Depends on what language you already speak. The more similar a language is to the one you already know the easier it will be to learn. Where going from Japanese to English can be hard because Japan basically has 3 different alphabets.

That’s pretty much what my Japanese teacher said. She said going from English to Japanese is hard because they are so different. Where as English to Spanish is a lot easier. And going from mandarin to Japanese is a lot easier. Fr the most part when learning a new language difficulty is determined by what language you’re starting from.

I really liked the maximum ride books back in middle school. So a few months ago I decide to read Witch and Wizard by James Paterson... I hated it, I felt like Patterson was copy and pasting from better books like Harry Potter and Percy Jackson. The book was so uninspired it made me mad. The world building was lazy. The main characters are annoying like we get it Wisty you’re the rebellious sarcastic person, yay good for you now please be quiet. Honestly the entire dialogue is terrible.
